title: Northstar priorities: 3-month orbit + All-Hands guide (v0.1)
summary: Draft compact to align leadership and org on Northstar priorities for the upcoming 12 weeks, with a 90-minute All-Hands runbook and slide/script checklist for exec updates. Focus: cost/perf controls, Private deployment readiness, and developer experience milestones.
body:
Purpose:
This doc is the working plan for a tight 3-month cycle ("quarterlike" sprint) that stitches OKR drafts, an exec briefing for the leadership team, and the All-Hands run of show. Goal is to converge on 3 company-level priorities that cascade to teams and to have a repeatable All-Hands playbook that communicates tradeoffs clearly (cost vs latency vs reliability).

High-level Northstar candidates (proposed):
1) Inference Economics: reduce hosted per-token cost by 20% while holding 95th-p99 latency SLOs.
   - Why: unit cost is the primary buyer objection for scale customers; must show measurable runway improvements.
   - Owner: Marco Nguyen (platform economics)

2) Private and Dedicated Expansion: complete 2 pilot Private customer deployments (VPC + on-prem) and ship dedicated autoscale policies for Reserved Capacity.
   - Why: enterprise demand + ARR motion rely on low-friction Private options and predictable Dedicated SLAs.
   - Owner: Dana Thompson (sales eng + private deployments)

3) Developer Experience & Observability: launch the new cost/latency tracing UI and baseline SDK ergonomics for tool-calling and streaming across hosted/dedicated/private.
   - Why: lower time-to-first-success for engineers reduces churn and accelerates PLG expansion.
   - Owner: Priya Kapoor (devx + console)
body_continued:
Draft company-level OKRs (for discussion):
Objective A — Make inference predictable and 20% cheaper for scale apps
KR A1: Reduce average per-token serving cost for top-50 customers by 20% (metrics in GA).
KR A2: Implement and roll out automatic KV-prefix caching that reduces redundant compute by 15% for conversational workloads.
KR A3: Add two quantization profiles validated on customer prompts with < 1% quality regression.

Objective B — Enterprise readiness: Private & Dedicated go-to-live
KR B1: Complete 2 Private pilot deliveries (one VPC, one on-prem) that pass compliance checklist.
KR B2: Ship Dedicated autoscaler + burst policy and validate under 3 load patterns with SRE-run chaos.
KR B3: Put KMS/HSM integration into GA for Private customers.

Objective C — Developer velocity and observability
KR C1: Ship revamped Console trace view; adoption: 30% of active teams use traces within 6 weeks.
KR C2: Reduce mean time to integration (first gen sample app to production call) from 4 days to 24 hours (measured across new signups).
KR C3: Add 5 monitoring alerts tied to quality regression signals and reduce noisefloor by 40%.

Notes on KR scoping: these KRs are intentionally outcome-oriented; each engineering area should propose implementation-level milestones for sprint planning.

Alignment checkpoints & milestones (90-day cadence):
- Week 0: Leadership sync (this doc) + finalize owners and resource ask.
- Week 1–2: Tech spike and cost audit (Platform + Serving Runtime). Deliverable: cost baseline dashboard.
- Week 3–6: Implementation waves (concurrent): caching + autoscaling + console traces. Weekly demos at Eng All-Hands.
- Week 7–9: Pilot rollouts (Private pilot 1, Dedicated autoscale dogfood).
- Week 10–12: Harden, measure KRs, prep All-Hands company report.

Resource & risk notes: 
- Resource ask: +1 infra SRE rotation, +0.6 FE for console sprint, contract engineer for quantization validation (8 weeks).
- Risks: quality regressions from quantization, network egress during Private deployments, billing anomalies from experimental batching. Mitigations: staged rollouts, regression evals, and billing playbook.

All-Hands (90-minute) runbook (draft):
- Format: 15m company state + 30m product/tech deep dives (3x10m) + 20m customer stories + 15m leadership Q&A + 10m closing and calls-to-action.
- Prework for presenters (due Week 10): 1-slide TL;DR and 3 supporting slides (metrics, customer impact, clear ask). Put slides in GH PR for review.
- Slide checklist (mandatory): one baseline metric snapshot, one concrete customer example, one engineer-level rollout plan, one CTA for the org.
- Moderation: Evan Ross to host; exec intros kept to 2 minutes each.
- Q&A format: Collect questions in #all-hands-questions Slack channel 48h prior; live upvotes will surface top 6.

Exec update script template (1 page each):
- 30s headline: "What changed since last update" (metric + story).
- 60s status: "On track / at risk" + one mitigation.
- 30s ask: "What I need from org in the next 2 weeks" (people, decisions, experiments).

Communication & cascade plan: 
- Immediate: this doc + short survey to leads (owner confirmation + resource gaps) by EOD Week 0.
- Week 2: consolidated OKR calendar + team-level mapping in Confluence (owner: product-ops).
- Week 6: mid-sprint check-in email from CEO with highlights and corrections.
- Post 90-day: scorecard published, winners/learning, and retrospective notes.

Measurement & dashboards:
- Primary dashboard owners: Platform (cost), Console (observability), Product Ops (adoption).
- Required panels: cost per token by model type, p50/p95/p99 latency over last 7 days, Private deployment throughput, SDK integration time histogram.

Open decisions (needs leadership input):
1) Tradeoff policy for quality vs cost: acceptable regression cap (propose 1% on user-facing metrics).
2) Prioritization of Private pilot customers (security-sensitive vs high-volume).
3) Headcount reprioritization for Q1: can we borrow 0.6 FE from Growth?

Action items (next 7 days):
- All owners confirm ownership and allocate tentative milestones (Aisha).
- Platform: publish cost baseline and expected savings hypotheses (Marco).
- Private deployments: propose 2 pilot customer candidates and compliance gating checklist (Dana).
- DevX: draft console trace storyboard and API surface notes (Priya).
- Comm: draft All-Hands calendar invite and Slack pre-ask for Qs (Evan).

Appendix: audience-ready talking points (for execs)
- Headline: "Our plan for the next 90 days focuses on making inference cheaper, more private, and faster to integrate — measurable wins for customers and predictable economics for growth."
- 3 bullets for product: cost-first optimizations, private delivery momentum, console improvements driving faster adoption.
- 2 bullets for eng: prioritize safe rollouts with regression gating and automated metrics checks.
- CTA for company: "Volunteer for demo days; nominate customer stories; help with chaos test coverage."

Versioning notes: v0.1 — early working draft for leadership discussion. Expect v0.2 after leadership sync (Week 0 meeting).
